text:
maya: Heads up — after the k8s 1.28 rollout in eu-west-1 a few of our GPU node pools aren't scaling. Multiple pods Pending > 10m. Anyone seeing this?
sam: Yep seeing it. Pods show `0/1` resources and autoscaler logs show errors like 'no nodegroup found for labels'. pasted tail of CA log below:
```
E0321 11:02:03.123456 1 autoscaler.go:324] Failed to find node group for labels: map[kubernetes.io/hostname:ip-10-0-1-234 node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass:gpupool-eu-west]
E0321 11:02:03.123789 1 scale.go:211] skipping scale up, no matching node group
```
liam: That `node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass` label looks new — CCM changed how it advertises nodeClass when we switched to the new cloud-controller-manager image. CA is still matching on our old label selector in node-group config.
maya: I ran `kubectl get nodes --show-labels | rg gpupool` — nodes do have both `node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=gpupool-eu-west` and `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=g4dn.xlarge`. But autoscaler config uses `--node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled` plus a label-matching heuristic that doesn't look at the new custom key.
simon: We hit a label rename race: CCM 0.9.1 switched to publishing the nodeClass under our org prefix to avoid clashing with other clouds. Cluster-autoscaler upstream didn't account for that — our CA expects either `node-role.kubernetes.io/` or cloud-provider labels.
sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) patch CA to check additional label key, 2) add legacy label back on nodes via daemonset, or 3) bump min nodes for affected gpupools temporarily. 1) is least invasive if we can push a small shim.
liam: I'll prepare a tiny autoscaler-side shim that treats `node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass` as equivalent to `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type` for discovery. Should be a <10-line change in our fork.
maya: Go for it. Meanwhile I'm going to increase min for `gpupool-eu-west-1` from 0->1 to avoid customer impact (costs noted).
sam: FYI pods in namespace `inference-prod` are the immediate customers blocked. Scaling events spiked because several training jobs came in right after upgrade.
simon: Cost estimate: +1 node for 24h in that pool ~ $48/day, plus risk of extra preemptible replacements. I'll approve emergency bump.
liam: Pushing shim now to staging. Deploy command:
```bash
kubectl -n infra set image deployment/autoscaler autoscaler=gcr.io/redwood/autoscaler-shim:hotfix-ccm-label
```
deploy-bot: Started rollout of `autoscaler-shim:hotfix-ccm-label` to infra/staging (id: deploy-2026-03-21-1105).
deploy-bot: Rollout successful: 1/1 updated, 0 errors.
sam: After shim, CA logs show it's matching gpupool groups again:
```
I0321 11:15:07.987 1 autoscaler.go:410] Found node group for labels: node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=gpupool-eu-west -> gpupool-eu-west (min:1,max:10)
I0321 11:16:12.456 1 scale_up.go:78] Triggering scale up: 1 node(s) for gpupool-eu-west
```
maya: Verified a new node joined and Pending pods are progressing. Thanks.
liam: I'll promote the shim to prod after a quick canary and open a PR with tests to make CA accept both old and new keys. Also adding e2e that simulates label rename.
simon: Please include a note in the upgrade playbook: CCM renames we use (nodeclass -> node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass) must be included in autoscaler discovery docs.
maya: Filed `INFRA-4821` with root cause + remediation steps + rollback plan. cc @sre @platform.
sam: :thumbsup:
maya: Postmortem will be a short writeup, but immediate followups: 1) prod shim rollout, 2) playbook update, 3) add daemonset that can add legacy labels if needed for future rollbacks.
liam: Rolling to prod now. Deploy command same as above but `-n infra` and image `gcr.io/redwood/autoscaler-shim:hotfix-ccm-label-prod`
deploy-bot: Started rollout of `autoscaler-shim:hotfix-ccm-label-prod` (id: deploy-2026-03-21-1132).
deploy-bot: Rollout successful across eu-west-1 clusters.
maya: Back to green for GPUs in eu-west-1, keeping min=1 for 2 hours to be safe. Will revert min later.
simon: Thanks team. We'll track cost and flip min back once stable.
